title: Run spec
description: Everything fixed about one run: one worker host carrying out this spec from start to finish. Every field is required but four, added after the first campaigns ran, so the specs they recorded stay valid and unchanged: procedure.release_after_ready_s is 0 when absent, workload.chromium_extra_flags (the whole workload section may be left out) is no extra flags, microvm.console is verbose and microvm.memory_pages is 4k. Values that follow from other fields (the host kind, the host's vCPUs and price) are never fields. docs/spec.md explains each field and the rules expand.py checks beyond this schema.

virtio_rng.x-message: Cloud Hypervisor always has a random-number device, so this must be true

worker_host.description: The EC2 instance whose capacity the run measures.

instance_type.description: The worker host's EC2 instance type. Its host kind (metal or nested), vCPUs, memory and price follow from it (instance-types.json).

hypervisor.description: The program on the worker host that runs each microVM, and how it presents devices to the guest.

virtio_transport.description: How each microVM's virtio devices reach its guest kernel. Firecracker can use either; Cloud Hypervisor only pci.

virtio_rng.description: Whether each microVM has a virtio random-number device. A choice for Firecracker; Cloud Hypervisor always has one.

microvm.description: The size of each microVM, what its guest kernel prints to the console as it boots, and how its memory is backed. The guest it boots and the task it runs are the same in every run.

console.description: What each guest kernel prints on its serial console while it boots. verbose prints the whole kernel log, about 21 KB, as every run before this field did. quiet adds `quiet loglevel=3` to the kernel command line, so only critical kernel messages print (a panic or oops still prints in full); errors, warnings and the rest stay in the kernel's own log. quiet-i8042 adds Firecracker's own `i8042.noaux i8042.nomux i8042.dumbkbd` too, so the kernel skips probing the emulated PS/2 keyboard (Cloud Hypervisor's guests find no PS/2 controller, so there it boots as quiet does). Every character the guest prints costs host CPU in the hypervisor's emulated serial port. Optional: absent is verbose.

memory_pages.description: How the hypervisor asks the worker host to back each microVM's guest memory. 4k asks for nothing, as every run before this field did: 4 KiB pages unless the host's transparent huge page mode is always. thp asks for transparent huge pages (Firecracker's huge_pages Transparent, Cloud Hypervisor's thp=on), which the host grants when its mode is always or madvise. run.json records the host's mode. Optional: absent is 4k.

densities.description: The densities to test, in increasing order. A trial at density N starts N microVMs at the same moment. Make the steps fine where the host is expected to fail: a result is only as precise as the step between the last pass and the first failure.

criteria.description: What a trial must meet to pass, besides every microVM ready, every task succeeding and nothing left on the host.

step_p50_target_ms.description: For each of the five steps, the median over the trial's tasks must be at most this.

step_p95_target_ms.description: For each of the five steps, the 95th percentile over the trial's tasks must be at most this.

task_p95_target_ms.description: The 95th percentile of whole-task time over the trial's tasks must be at most this.

ready_timeout_s.description: Every microVM must report its browser ready within this many seconds of being started.

step_timeout_ms.description: A step that takes longer than this fails its task.

task_timeout_ms.description: A task that takes longer than this fails.

procedure.description: How the run steps through its densities. The order, the stop at the first failing density, the warm-up and the illustration are the same in every run (docs/method.md).

trials_per_density.description: Trials at each density on the way up.

boundary_trials.description: Extra trials, once the run stops going up, at the highest passing density and at the lowest failing one, to check the result holds.

settle_s.description: Seconds the worker host sits idle before every trial, so the last trial's cleanup is finished.

release_after_ready_s.description: Seconds every trial waits, once all its microVMs are ready, before it releases their tasks together. 0 releases them the moment the last microVM is ready, while browsers may still be finishing startup (a cold start); a wait measures a warm pool, whose microVMs are ready and idle when the tasks arrive. Task times start at the release, so the wait is in no task's time. Optional: absent is 0.

support_host.description: The separate instance that serves the test shopping site and collects telemetry, one per run.

instance_type.description: The support host's EC2 instance type. A bigger worker host needs a bigger support host, so the support host is never what runs out.

workload.description: How each microVM's browser is configured. The guest, the five-step task and the test site are the same in every run. Optional: absent is no extra flags.

items.x-message: a flag is --name or --name=value, in plain ASCII, at most 200 characters

chromium_extra_flags.description: Chromium flags added after the base flags every run has, to compare browser configurations. Each must be on the allowed list in chromium-flags.json, which says why it is allowed: it may change how Chromium spends memory and CPU, never what a task does. Each flag once, at most 8, at most 512 characters together. Optional: absent is none.
